pulse_audit.independent_method: For each planned pulse, match unique onset/offset and current analyser samples. Admitted captures require RMS >=0.25, audioAt in onset..offset+250ms, and captureAt-audioAt in 0..100ms. Match those source IDs to received/stage timestamps inside the common interval and recompute first response delay, <=1000ms delivery and every published count.
pulse_audit.limitations: Source lineage and sampled waveform RMS do not establish visible beat strength, semantic prompt correctness or artistic response. Uncaptured is a subset of unobserved, not an additional independent loss. N01 admission-promotion gates were not imposed on N06.

visual_sample.limits: Samples are the first received JPEG stored for each audioLevel during measurement, not necessarily the same input phase across trials and not frames selected from the later stall episode. This is a gross-corruption check only; no pixel/perceptual/cross-worker/temporal equivalence or human artistic approval is implied.

important_limits_retained: Selected/baseline is a configuration bundle; one/two active-worker contrasts run sequentially. Throughput differences are not causal attribution of every stall to GPUs.
Stage FPS counts source frames submitted to WebGL, not physical presentation; actual stage raster can be larger than generated dimensions.
Age uses local capture encode start to the named boundary. Worker stats arrival gaps are observed at the client, not direct measurements of GPU execution gaps.
Medians of per-trial percentiles and matched-ratio medians are distinct from pooled percentiles and ratios of cell medians; worst tails remain explicit.
Both models loaded on the same two-GPU host; all shapes qualified before formal timing and caches seeded from completed same-stack proof. No cold-start performance conclusion.
Cross-process, physical-GPU, dependency and cache-history differences prevent attributing old/new-stack pixel or FPS changes solely to Torch.
Same-process terminal-skip/output-cast production proof does not directly prove the full live constant-cache/event wrapper or cross-worker pixel equivalence.
